The test image shows a corn plant with one completely bleached/white leaf while surrounding leaves are green. The white leaf appears entirely blanched. I also notice some browning at the stalk area. This distinctive pattern narrows candidates to bacterial diseases causing bleaching: Goss's Wilt, Stewart's Disease, or possibly others.

Let me check reference images for my top candidates.
Goss's Wilt and Stewart's Disease don't match - they show brown streaking/wilting, not a completely bleached white leaf. Let me check Crazy Top which can cause leaf bleaching.
Crazy Top shows different symptoms. The completely bleached single leaf is distinctive. Let me check one more candidate - Northern Leaf Blight or Corn Stunt Spiroplasma.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image features:**
- One large leaf is completely white/bleached (uniformly, no spots or streaks)
- Rest of the corn plant is green and appears relatively healthy at ear-formation stage
- Stalk shows some brownish discoloration near the ear node
- Ear of corn visible on the left

**Reference comparisons:**
- **Goss's Wilt**: Shows brown/tan necrotic streaks with yellow-green wavy margins — doesn't match complete bleaching
- **Stewart's Disease**: Shows complete plant wilting and browning — doesn't match single-leaf bleaching
- **Crazy Top**: Shows twisted/rolled leaves and can cause complete leaf bleaching in infected plants — partial match
- **Corn Stunt Spiroplasma**: Shows purple/tan husk discoloration with black dots — doesn't match

The completely uniform white/bleached single leaf on an otherwise green plant is the dominant feature. Crazy Top (Sclerophthora macrospora) can cause complete leaf blanching/whitening, especially in upper leaves, which is the closest match among the candidates I've evaluated. The stalk discoloration is also consistent.
